summary:
[FRAGMENT] 

[...] of these and couldn’t sell them because there was no market here for them, and so you returned them. In fact no market existed anywhere on Earth for them. At the LACon last August David Hartwell approached me and asked permission for him and Paul Williams to print 2,000 hardcover copies of an old experimental novel of mine which you tried so hard to sell (you sure worked your ass off; I saw the list of those who’d seen it and rejected it when you returned the ms to me), splitting any profits but assuming all the costs them­ selves (CONFESSIONS OF A CRAP ARTIST, it was called). You see, Paul Wil­ liams and I had become friends several years ago, and I had mentioned having written 10 non-s-f novels no one would buy, and he asked for one that I person­ ally liked, so I gave him the ms for CONFESSIONS—he carted it all over New York, with no luck, but now they themselves, Williams and Hartwell, are putting it out and feel that even though they will make no profit, it might start an inter­ est in my experimental novels. 

Okay, Scott: here’s my thought. I have a fair idea of where the heads of these Storm-Rottensteiner-Bengston are at, regarding what it is they, over there, like about my work. For example, Goran tells me in his book of critical essays on post-World War Two U.S. writers his study of me doesn’t put me into an s- f class but more of a black humor class.
